## Anomaly
{"kind": "fun", "system": "serverscriptservice/cashinservice.luau", "severity": "medium", "title": "[ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau] Sounds are effectively silent. The census shows sounds_played=0 and client_sounds_played=0 even though the counter sounds_played is 15, and the sound is a per-part Sound parented to the collector with Volume 0.5 and a SoundId from config. It may be failing to", "expected": "Send the cash-in event to the client, which plays a 2D Sound in SoundService using the verified coin sound id from GameAssets sounds. Set Volume to 0.8 and PlaybackSpeed from pitchForTier, and use SoundService:PlayLocalSound or a Sound with Parent=SoundService. Keep the server Sound only as a fallback. Count client_sounds_played.", "observed": "Sounds are effectively silent. The census shows sounds_played=0 and client_sounds_played=0 even though the counter sounds_played is 15, and the sound is a per-part Sound parented to the collector with Volume 0.5 and a SoundId from config. It may be failing to load, or it is too quiet and only server-side, so the main reward (cha-ching) is not audible.", "path": "ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "The coin asset is not broken: rbxasset://sounds/volume_slider.ogg loads and plays, and the server-created CashInLocalSound in PlayerGui reaches IsPlaying=true. The failure is in the client feedback path. CashInFx.client.luau findRemote calls WaitForChild(name, 10) on ReplicatedStorage.Remotes, but that folder holds only RebirthRequest and RebirthResult. CashInService creates CashIn and PurchaseFx at the ReplicatedStorage root. The client therefore blocks about 10 seconds before it falls back to the root, and the purchase remote waits another 10 seconds, so early cash-ins reach no client handler. Once connected, onCashIn plays a 3D sound on a temporary anchor at Volume 0.4 with RollOffMaxDistance 120, not a 2D coin sound at 0.8. It also never increments any client_sounds_played counter, which is why that census reads 0. The only audible path is the server fallback Sound in PlayerGui.", "file": "StarterPlayerScripts/CashInFx.client.luau", "evidence": "Probe 4: the coin and config ids both load, and a plain Sound reports IsPlaying=true. CASHIN_REMOTE is 'CashIn' and ReplicatedStorage.CashIn exists. Probe 5: ReplicatedStorage.Remotes contains only RebirthRequest and RebirthResult, while CashIn and PurchaseFx sit at the root. The server's CashInLocalSound instances in PlayerGui are loaded, and one is playing at Volume 0.8. Reading CashInFx.client.luau shows the 10s WaitForChild in findRemote, a 3D playSound at 0.4 volume, and no client sound counter.", "fix_hint": 

Probe (Client): Check whether the config and GameAssets sound ids load and play, and whether the remote exists where the client looks for it
```luau
local RS=game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local C=require(RS.CashInConfig)
local GA=require(RS.GameAssets)
local out={cfgId=tostring(C.CASHIN_SOUND_ID),popId=tostring(C.POP_SOUND_ID),vol=C.CASHIN_VOLUME,coin=GA.Sounds.Coin,remote=C.CASHIN_REMOTE}
local res={}
for _,id in ipairs({tostring(C.CASHIN_SOUND_ID),GA.Sounds.Coin}) do
 local s=Instance.new('Sound') s.SoundId=id s.Volume=0.8 s.Parent=game:GetService('SoundService')
 local t=os.clock()
 while not s.IsLoaded and os.clock()-t<2 do task.wait(0.1) end
 s:Play() task.wait(0.2)
 res[id]={loaded=s.IsLoaded,len=s.TimeLength,playing=s.IsPlaying}
 s:Destroy()
end
out.res=res
local pg=game.Players.LocalPlayer.PlayerGui
local n=0 for _,d in ip
```

## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().

```luau
-- check: Touching an affordable buy pad takes its price and marks it bought
-- covers: anomaly: buy pads never unlock
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local t0 = os.clock()
while not (p and p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do
	task.wait(0.5)
	p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
end
if not p or not p.Character then error("setup: no player character within 10s") end
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local pad = workspace:FindFirstChild("BuyPad_dropper2", true)
if not pad then error("setup: no BuyPad_dropper2 in workspace") end
local hrp = p.Character.HumanoidRootPart
local oldCash, oldCF = cash.Value, hrp.CFrame
cash.Value = 1000
hrp.CFrame = pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
local t1 = os.clock()
while cash.Value == 1000 and os.clock() - t1 < 3 do task.wait(0.1) end
local spent = 1000 - cash.Value
cash.Value, hrp.CFrame = oldCash, oldCF
return { ok = spent == 25, detail = "pad took " .. spent .. " cash, expected 25" }
```
